author: Rachel Estrada
title: Gov. Abbott breaks silence on fatal ICE shooting of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, confirms Texas Rangers investigation - NewsBreak
text:
By Rachel Estrada ,
4 hours ago HOUSTON (CW39) – In Houston Wednesday afternoon, Gov. Greg Abbott addressed the fatal shooting of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo publicly for the first time, confirming the Texas Rangers will investigate alongside federal officials while defending continued immigration enforcement in Texas communities.
What to Know Abbott spoke publicly in Houston Wednesday, first comments since the shooting Confirmed Texas Rangers meeting with federal officials and Houston police Rangers will investigate independently, according to Abbott DHS says Salgado Araujo was not the intended target Abbott says immigration laws can be enforced “without shooting people” Abbott addressed his silence on this compared to his past Minneapolis comments Why did Gov. Abbott address his silence on the shooting? Gov. Abbott addressed his lack of public comment on the shooting, having previously been vocal about the Minneapolis unrest. He acknowledged the tragedy first.
“Any loss of life is tragic,” Abbott said. “Everyone in Texas wants to ensure there’s no loss of life.”
What did Abbott confirm about the fatal ICE shooting investigation? Abbott said that the Texas Department of Public Safety and the Texas Rangers have met with federal officials and the Houston Police Department. He confirmed the Rangers will now investigate the shooting alongside federal authorities.
“The Texas Rangers are now going to be involved in an investigation of this matter, working alongside federal officials to get to the bottom of exactly what happened,” Abbott said.
Gov. Abbott also addressed whether the investigation would be independent, pointing to the Rangers’ reputation. “Anytime the Texas Rangers are involved, they work independently,” he said. “They’re well known, not just in the state of Texas, but elsewhere for their independence and in conducting investigations.”
Does the shooting change Abbott’s stance on immigration enforcement? Gov. Abbott also addressed whether the fatal ICE shooting of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo – which the Department of Homeland Security says was not the intended target – gave Gov. Abbott any pause about how enforcement operations are being carried out in Texas communities. Abbott maintained his support for continued enforcement while stressing safety.
“One thing we want to see in Texas and across America, we don’t want to see people shot, period,” Abbott said. “That’s separate from whether the immigration laws are going to be enforced. I fully expect our immigration laws to be enforced.”
Abbott argued the two goals aren’t in conflict. “It’s proven the immigration laws can be enforced and stopping illegal immigration from coming across the border can be achieved without shooting people,” he said.
What did Abbott say about law enforcement’s responsibility? Abbott spoke about what he called the top priority for all law enforcement agencies operating in Texas, addressing concerns that people are being shot without officers properly identifying their targets first.
“The goal for law enforcement, whether you be Houston Police Department, Texas Department of Public Safety or federal law enforcement, is first thing – don’t kill people,” Abbott said. “But you can achieve that goal while at the very same time making sure you’re enforcing immigration laws.”
What happens next? The Texas Rangers’ investigation now moves forward alongside federal officials and Houston police, following the joint request from Mayor John Whitmire and Houston Police Chief Noe Diaz earlier this week.
Houston Mayor to monitor independent investigation Mayor John Whitmire also continued his call for transparency and stronger federal oversight of ICE, including body cameras and expanded training, following the fatal shooting of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo and the launch of a Texas Rangers investigation into the case.
“The public deserves transparency and accountability whenever a person’s life is taken by a law enforcement agency. Governor Abbott made the right decision to involve the Texas Rangers in the investigation of the fatal shooting of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo following a direct request by Houston Police Chief Noe Diaz and me on Tuesday. At a time like this, we must set aside politics and partisanship and focus on the facts. At the same time, the federal government must do its part by requiring body cameras and stronger training for ICE officers to help transparency, accountability, and public trust, as we do with the Houston Police Department.
My office and HPD will continue to assist the Harris County District Attorney, the Rangers, DHS-OIG, the FBI, and all agencies involved as they conduct a thorough and independent investigation.”
